content: I want to set up a cache for Physlib, so we can use the new lake cache feature. From what I understand there isn't good documentation coverage for this yet. I was wondering if anyone who has done this for a repo, or knows the inner workings, would be able to give a brief list of steps as a starting point?

I haven't managed to do this yet, but I think I have a much better conceptual framework of what lake cache is doing. Many thanks to @Kim Morrison and @Joscha Mennicken for help over dm. In case it helps anyone, I'm going to write a simple version here (mainly for myself).

The cache works by storing information in an online S3 bucket (basically a way to store data over the internet).

To be able to read and write the cache lake needs to know where the cache is stored (i.e. the location of the bucket). This is controlled by a.toml file (but not lakefile.toml). The location of this toml file is stored by an environment variable LAKE_CONFIG (defaults to ~/.lake/config.toml if unset). The command lake cache services --help tells one what it should look like. It seems like there are two approaches to this toml file. Generate it as part of the workflow (downside to me here seems that this prevents people using the cache locally), or store it somewhere in the repo (the location of the cache is public information so this is fine). (I'm not sure the exact reason why this configuration information cannot be just stored in lakefile.toml.)

For the cache to make sense securely, we need only people (or GitHub workflows) with special privileges to be able to write to it. This is controlled by an environment variable LAKE_CACHE_KEY which is a secret but can be stored as part GitHub repo as an encrypted secret - but is never stored in the GitHub files itself.

The environment variables LAKE_CONFIG and LAKE_CACHE_KEY are about the bucket. There are some other ones that are related to local information LAKE_CACHE_DIR is where the cache lives, LAKE_ARTIFACT_CACHE is about whether a build can write to a cache and LAKE_RESTORE_ARTIFACTS is about whether to copy cached oleans back into the main build.

Claude drew this ascii art the help visualise it: 

        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │   REMOTE S3 bucket  (config.toml URLs)  │
        └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
              ▲ lake cache put          │ lake cache get
              │  (signed, KEY)          ▼  (anonymous)
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │   LOCAL cache dir   =  LAKE_CACHE_DIR   │
        │   (content-addressed olean store)       │
        └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
              ▲ write: LAKE_ARTIFACT_CACHE      │ materialize: LAKE_RESTORE_ARTIFACTS
              │                                 ▼
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │   lake build  ⇄  .lake/build/*.olean    │
        └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
